name: Lucius
overview: Lucius is a male figure recognized in the New Testament as a prophet and teacher in the early Christian community at Antioch. His role highlights his spiritual leadership and contribution to the church's growth during a formative period. No additional tribal or familial details are provided in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Lucius appears without a given meaning in the biblical text. He is also referred to as Lucius of Cyrene, indicating his geographical origin rather than a titular meaning. The names serve primarily to identify him without conveying specific theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Lucius beyond his identification as a prophet and teacher in Antioch. There are no listed relatives or connections detailed in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Lucius holds significance as one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, a key center for early Christian mission and discipleship. His presence among the leaders there underscores the Spirit-led foundation of the church's ministry. By serving in this capacity, Lucius contributed to the spreading of the gospel and the nurturing of the early Christian community.
